title: Laser Squad
build: Blade Software's 48K tape (TOSEC: Laser Squad (1988)(Blade)[scenario 1-2].tzx and [scenario 3-5].tzx): a BASIC loader, the loading screen, the 22,521-byte engine at $5E28-$B620 and five headerless scenario blocks of 18,911 bytes each, loaded at $B621-$FFFF
uncounted: loaded with the game, excluded by default as screen RAM

records.c: The engine's first instruction: the interrupts off for good, the variables at $5B00-$5E25 cleared, the border black, the stack at $5E39, and the main menu ($B1C3).
A NOP that is the bottom of the stack: the stack pointer is set to its address at every restart.
In a game against the computer ($B706 set), $5DF7 = the side whose turn it is: 1, the computer's, or 0, the player's.

A new game: the controls ($B0AD), one player or two ($A211); the first side equips its units ($9D55) and places them ($A370), then they come off the map; the second side does the same when a player has it. The second side's squares for placing are cleared ($A474), every unit put on the map, both sides' views set to the same corner and cursor ($B707-$B70E), the units of turn 0 arrive ($A2EE), and the turns begin.
The turns, for good: the menu between turns ($B1F7), the turn's number ($B711) on by one, the units of this turn arrived ($A2EE), each side's half-turn, and whether the game is over ($A4A4).

A side's half-turn ($B712 the side). Each of its units starts it afresh: its most action points ($05) are its own ($1B) less what its load costs ($19), and its points ($06) those less its wounds' share ($6B29) and its $11.
In the first side's half-turn, each unit's count at $B63A + its number goes down by one, to 0.
Stamina ($0A): the action points it did not spend last time ($22), short of half its most, come back to it, up to its full ($09); those it spent beyond half are taken from it, down to 0.
With stamina under $20, half the action points; and never fewer than a tenth of the most.
The map as the side sees it, the side's own view and cursor, and its move: the scenario's computer player ($B621) or the player's turn screen and cursor mode.
The side's view and cursor kept, the scenario's end of a half-turn ($B630), the fuses ($9C8B), and the next side.
HL = the side's view and cursor: four bytes at $B707 + 4 x side, the view's corner and the cursor's square.
The screen a player's half-turn begins with: message $54, the side's name (scenario message $A0 or $A1), the turn's number, the turns left ($B701 less it) and the scores; fire to play.
The scores: message $68, and each side's victory points and name (the scenario's messages $A0 and $A1) on rows 16 and 19.
Clear the screen to black: A = 0, then on into clearScreenA.
Clear the screen to the colours in A: the attributes filled with A from $5AFF down to $5800, then the pixels cleared from $57FF down to $4000.
The screen address of the top line of each of the 24 character rows, a word each, for printChar and drawTile.

Print character A at the character row in PRINT_ROW and the column in PRINT_COL: its eight bytes from the font at $B139 + 8 x A, then the cell's attribute from ATTR. HL, DE and AF are kept; B is 0 on return.
The attribute's address from the screen address of the cell's last line.

Draw tile A, two characters by two (16 x 16 pixels), at the row in PRINT_ROW and the column in PRINT_COL. The tile's 32 bytes are at $E8DF + 32 x A, kept in TILE_GFX: the top left cell's 8 bytes, then the top right, the bottom left and the bottom right. All four cells take the colours in ATTR.
DE: the screen address of the tile's top row; BC: of the row under it, the next entry in screenRows.
The attributes, from the bottom right cell back to the top left.
Copy 8 bytes from DE down one character cell from screen address HL (HL kept, DE on past them).

HL = the map's square at row E and column D: $D6BF + 80 x E + D. The map is 80 squares across and 50 down, one byte each: a terrain type below $6E, an object from $6E to $8B, a unit from $8C to $9F. Returns DE = $D6BF and A = the column.

Draw the view: the 11 x 11 squares of the map from the row in VIEW_ROW and the column in VIEW_COL, row by row, at character rows and columns 1 to 21 (a square is a tile of two characters by two). Clears $B715 first, the flag hideView sets when it blanks the view. MAP_PTR walks the map, PRINT_ROW and PRINT_COL the screen.
On to the next row of the map: 80 squares on from the row's start, so 69 on from its end.
Draw the map's square A at PRINT_ROW and PRINT_COL: the scenario's table of squares at the address in $B716 holds two bytes for each, its colours (into ATTR) and its tile (drawTile).
Draw the view as drawView does, column by column: what the scroll routine draws after moving the view across.
Back to the top of the next column: 11 rows of 80 up, one square on.

One step of cursor mode. The cursor blinks while the controls are read, on for 255 turns and off for 140 ($B71A counts them down, $5D16 says whether it is on show); each turn it moves if a way is held (moveCursor), and the square under it is described when it stops (squareReadout). Returns at the first turn nothing moves it. Every register is kept.
A short wait, 120 turns of DJNZ.
Aim: the crosshair blinks (every 256 turns, counted by $5D17) and moves with the controls, faster the longer a way is held, until fire is pressed. Every register is kept.
Blink the crosshair: $5D1A says whether it is drawn, and drawCrosshair draws it with XOR, so drawing it again takes it off.

Move the crosshair a square: off it comes and the cursor's square moves (readMove). If the view scrolled it is left off; otherwise it is drawn again after a wait that shortens as the way is held (the first step waits 200 delays more).
The crosshair's wait: 12 turns of a loop of ($5D1B), 256 for 0, which is then 6 shorter, down to 8.

The readout under the view. When the cursor stops ($5D10 clear until then) the square under it is described: infoText 3, then squareInfo, unless $A36F is set. When it moves again, the description is cleared (infoText 3) and there is a pause of 160 delays.
Wait 3 turns of a loop of 255 DJNZs (3,351 T-states a turn). BC is kept.
Wait 1 turn.
Wait 40 turns.
Wait 200 turns.
Move the cursor by the controls (readMove) and, if a way was held, show it (showMove).

Move the cursor's square a step for each way held in the controls ($5D2A): up, down, right and left, in that order. At the cursor's edge of the view the view moves instead. $5D1D is set if any way was held, $5D1E counts them less one, $5D1C collects the ways the view scrolled and $5D13 keeps the cursor's square from before.
A step up, noted (noteMove). A is kept.
A step down, noted.
A step right, noted.
A step left, noted.
Note a way held: $5D1D set, $5D1E one more.
Set when the view has scrolled and has to be drawn again.

A step right: the cursor's column (CURSOR_COL) one on, unless it is at the view's last ($B718). There the view moves one right instead (VIEW_COL), unless it shows the map's last column already (VIEW_COL $45: 80 columns less the view's 11), and SCROLLED and bit 3 of $5D1C are set.
The step itself, and the cursor's square written back (the steps left, up and down end here too).
A step left, the same way: the view's first column is $B719, the map's VIEW_COL 0, and the bit of $5D1C bit 2.
The step left.
A step up: the view's first row $B719, the map's VIEW_ROW 0, bit 0 of $5D1C.
The step up.
A step down: the view's last row $B718, the map's VIEW_ROW $27 (50 rows less 11), bit 1 of $5D1C.
The step down.

Show the cursor's move. After a scroll the view is drawn again (scrollView) with the cursor on it; otherwise the cursor is drawn at its new square, the square it left is drawn again (drawSquareAt), and there is a pause of 80 delays. A cursor held against the map's edge is drawn and at once drawn over, as its old square is its new one.

Draw the view again after a scroll, through the jumps at $6418 by the ways in $5D1C less one: from the bottom row up after a scroll up (drawViewUp), from the right after a scroll left (drawViewLeft), by columns after a scroll right (drawViewColumns), and by rows after a scroll down. Up and down at once, $5D1C 3 or 7, draws nothing.
The jumps, three bytes each: up, down, up and down, left, up and left, down and left, all but right, right, up and right, down and right.
Draw the cursor, tile $AF in white on black ($47), at its square in the view: the character row and column twice the cursor's, plus one.
Take the cursor off by drawing the map's square under it, unless $B71B is set.
Draw the map's square at the view's square HL (L the row, H the column), with DE the map's square at the view's top left.
Draw the view from its bottom row up, each row from the left.
Back to the start of the row above: 91 squares back from this row's end.
Draw the view column by column from its right-hand column leftwards.
Back to the top of the column to the left: 881 squares back.

Print character A in double height at PRINT_ROW and PRINT_COL: each of the font's eight lines twice, down two character cells, the top cell in the colours in ATTR and the bottom one in ATTR2. Every register is kept.

Print message A of the list at ($5D1F), from the row and column in $5D05 and $5D06. The messages each end with '|' ($7C), and message A begins after the A-th one (the 256th for 0). In a message, a byte of $F1 or more is a code (textCode) and '/' a new line (newLine); any other is a character, if bit 2 of $5D09 is set, or else a word of the dictionary at ($5D07). The dictionary is a list of words the same way, each one followed by a space unless bit 1 is set; in a word, a byte from $80 up is a code and '/' a new line. HL, DE and BC are kept. $5D09, how text is printed: bit 0, a '/' is a space; 1, no space after a word; 2, the bytes are characters; 3, double height; 4, the text runs down.
A word of the dictionary: find it, and print it a character at a time ($5D0C walks it).
Print character A, in double height if bit 3 of $5D09 is set, and move on.
Move on one character: a column right, or with bit 4 of $5D09 a row down (two in double height).
A new line: the next row from where the line began ($5D05), two rows on in double height, or with bit 4 of $5D09 the next column; just a space with bit 0.

A code in a message, at HL. $FF and $FD: the engine's dictionary ($AC06); $FE: the scenario's (its address at $B724). $FC, $FB: characters off, on (bit 2 of $5D09); $FA, $F9: double height on, off (bit 3); $F8, $F7: downwards off, on (bit 4); $F4, $F3: the space after words on, off (bit 1); $F2, $F1: '/' as a space off, on (bit 0). $F6: the colours, from the byte after the code into ATTR (and in double height the next into ATTR2). $F5: the row and the column, from the two bytes after. $5D21 is left on the code's last byte.

The controls' auto-repeat. With nothing held, $5CFB is cleared and the routine returns at once. Otherwise it waits up to 110 turns of a short delay and a read of the controls (only 40 while the controls repeat, with $5CFB set), and returns early when they are let go.
Print the number A, 0 to 255, in three characters, the digits and then spaces, leaving PRINT_COL two on.
Print A, under 100, as two digits, the second without moving on.
Print the digit A and move on.
Print the character A and move on a column.
Print the character A where PRINT_ROW and PRINT_COL say, in double height if bit 3 of $5D09 is set, without moving on. HL is kept.
Print message A of the engine's list in double height (bit 3 of $5D09), in the colours $06 above and $46 below: the readout's lines under the view.
Print message A of the engine's list in the usual height and the colours as they are.
The engine's list of messages ($A64E) and its dictionary ($AC06), then printMessage.
The bottom line: messages 1 and 2 in the colour of the side whose turn it is ($B702 + the side in $B712), then in white on red the turn ($B711) and that side's victory points ($B70F + the side).
IX = the record of unit A: the units are $8C on in the map, 40 bytes each from $D39F. Returns A = the unit's number from 0, DE = 40 x A.
IX = the record of object A: the objects are $6E to $8B in the map, 20 bytes each from the address at $B728.
IY = the record of terrain A, 12 bytes each from the address at $B726. Byte $04 of a unit's record picks the byte of its terrain's record that is the cost of a step onto it ($FF: impassable).
$5D24 (and HL) = the map's square under the cursor: the view's corner plus the cursor's square, the row in the low byte.

Describe the square under the cursor in the readout, from the scenario's messages. $5CFA keeps the square. Terrain ($00-$6D) has a message of its own; an object ($6E-$8B) its own, under the message for the floor under it (floorUnder); a unit ($8C up) its name, what it holds, and what it stands on.
A unit: its name, the object in its hands (if any), and then the square it stands on, an object or terrain.
An object: the floor under it, and the object.

IY = the record of the scenario's object A, from 1, 6 bytes each from the address at $B72A: its kind, its row and column, the floor under it, its ammunition and the unit carrying it. Returns at once, with Z, for 0 (none).
Message A + 1 of the scenario's list in double height, in the colours $06 and $46, at the column in H and the row in L.
The same where $5D05 says: the scenario's list of messages at the address in $B722, its dictionary at the address in $B724.

Choose from the menu on show. It has ($5D2C) lines, and the one chosen ($5D2B, from 0) is lit (lightLine). Up and down move the light, from the last line round to the first and back, with the controls' auto-repeat; fire flashes the line four times, with sound effect 5 each time, and returns.
Fire: the flash.

Light the menu's line ($5D2B), or put it out: the attributes of its 8 cells across by 2 rows, from the address in $5D2D plus 64 x (the line + 1), have their ink and paper swapped and BRIGHT set. HL is kept.

Cursor mode, the heart of a player's turn: the bottom line, the view and the readout, then the cursor (cursorStep) until fire is pressed, and the menu for the square under it. A unit of the side whose turn it is that has action points left offers line 0 (select it); any unit offers line 1; lines 2 to 5 are always there. The choice runs its routine from the table at $6A35. Returns when the turn ends (endTurn).
Clear the readout: message 5.
Whether unit A can be selected: IX and $5D33 its record; Z if it is on the side whose turn it is (bit 0 of its byte $25 matches $B712) and its action points ($06) are not 0.

Open a menu: the cursor off, the readout cleared, message 6, no lines yet ($5D2C, their option numbers listed from $5B00 by the pointer at $5D31), the lines lit from attribute $5858, and the text from row 4, column 24.
Add option A to the menu's list. A is kept.
Run the routine the line chosen asks for: its option number, from the list at $5B00, picks a word of the table at HL, and the routine is jumped to, so that it returns to the caller.
The routines of cursor mode's menu, by option: select the unit ($6CB3), $8742, $840C, $8495, end the turn (endTurnMenu), and nothing ($6A6C).
Option 4: end the turn? A menu of two lines, no and yes. Yes ($6A6A) returns past this routine and past cursor mode too.
The two answers: no (noOption) and yes (endTurn).
Yes: two return addresses dropped, so the RET leaves cursor mode.
No: nothing.

Wait until no key and no control is held: the ROM's KEY-SCAN, then the controls. Not in the computer's turn ($5DF7 set). Each turn of the loop adds one to $5D9C, which the random numbers mix in. Every register is kept.

The selected unit's numbers (its record's address at $5D33), unless its $08 is 0: its name, a share of $07 less $08 by $18 (healthShare), $19, two words picked by the top three bits of $0C and of $0A, half of $05, and the panel (unitPanel).
Wait for any key: port $FE read with every half-row at once, each turn adding one to $5D9C. Then sound effect 0.
C = A divided by B, rounded to the nearest, A the remainder. B must not be 0.
A = ($07) less ($08) of the unit at IX, divided by its ($18), rounded.
The way the unit faces: message 11 of the engine's list, then message ($21) + 12 in characters, ($21) being its facing, 0 (up) to 7 clockwise.
$5D23 = the floor of the map's square at the address in $5D3A: terrain as it is; for a unit, the square it stands on (its byte $16); for an object, the floor under it (floorUnder).
Message A + 1 of the scenario's list at the column in H and the row in L, in double height, in the colours as they are.
A line of the panel at HL: message 21 of the engine's list (blanks), then over it the scenario's message A + 1 in yellow on black.

The selected unit's panel: the way it faces; its action points ($06) in double height; the object in its hands ($23, when $17 is not 0); the terrain it stands on ($16, or the floor under the object or unit there) and that terrain's byte $06; and the enemies in sight (seenCount). IX is left on the unit.

Select the unit on the square at the address in $5D2F: $5D26 its number, IX its record, and the list from $5C3C cleared. In a player's turn, a unit holding an object ($17) whose bit 6 of $25 is clear may, at random (a number below $34 drawn, below $20 and at least the unit's $0C), show message $61, set that bit and drop it (dropForced). Then the units it sees (findSeen, showSeen), its numbers, the view centred on it, and its square, action points and facing kept (keepPlace).

Option 0, the unit selected. It blinks, shown for 255 turns of the controls and then a black square for 130, while the controls move it, turn it or (fire) open its menu; until it is dead, has no action points, or a move cannot be paid for (unitInput gives Z).
One read of the controls for the unit selected: fire opens its menu ($78CD), up is a step forwards, down a step back, right and left a turn. With none held, Z if the unit is dead ($08 is 0).

The unit's tile in the table of squares at $E660 (two bytes a square; a unit's is the second of its pair): picked by its kind (byte $00 rotated right three times, through the table at the address in $B71C), the kind of object in its hands ($23 less $6D, when $17 is not 0) and its facing ($21), through the table at the address in $B71E, eight tiles to a row.
The action points last asked of payAP.
Pay B action points from the unit at IX: $5D35 is what would be left, and NC. With too few, message $14 and carry, and $5D37 is set.
Message A of the engine's list in the readout, with sound effect $0B, then wait for the controls (waitControls).
A pause of 600 delays, then the wait for the controls.
In a player's turn, wait up to 65 turns of 40 delays, returning as soon as any control is held.

Turn the unit right an eighth, for one action point: its facing and its tile, the units it sees, the view drawn again (unless $5D36 is set), then afterAction. With too few points, its numbers again and Z, which lets it go.
Turn the unit left an eighth, the same way.
Centre the view on the unit under the cursor (cursorSquare), within the map.
Centre the view on the square in $5D24.

Centre the view on the square in HL (L the row, H the column): its corner 5 squares up and left of it, from 0 to 69 across and 0 to 39 down, and the cursor on the square; the cursor shown at once. The view is drawn unless $5D36 is set.
A step forwards, the way the unit faces ($5D38 clear).
A step back, the way opposite ($5D38 set, which doubles the cost).

The square a step from the one in $5D24 the way A (0 up, then clockwise to 7): $5D3A the row, $5D3B the column, and $5D1E the step's extra cost, all from the table at $6EA7. Z if the square is off the map.
The eight ways: the change in row and column and the extra cost, 2 for a diagonal.

What a step onto the square at $5D3A costs, in $5D28, and whether it can be made, in $5D29. 0 or 3: an enemy is there (3 when the unit steps back, or stands on a unit itself); 4: a unit of its own side is there and their bytes $02 add up to 21 or more; 2: too few action points; 5: the step can be made. When the unit's kind cannot cross the terrain at all, $5D29 is the byte under the unit instead. The cost is the terrain's for the unit (its record at $B726, the byte picked by the unit's $04), plus an object's ($03 of its record), plus the step's extra, doubled for a step back. $5D39 keeps what the square holds, $5D27 the floor, $5D3E the square's address, and $5D3C an enemy's record.

Make the step: the scenario's hook at $B62D; the action points paid ($06) and added to $22; the unit off its old square (its floor put back) and onto the new one; the units it sees, the view, and sound effect 3 in a player's turn. With no points left on a square another unit of its side shares (shared, $9A16) the unit goes back where it was kept (undoMove). Then, in the computer's turn, the hook at $B62A, or the view shown with a pause when $B715 is set. NZ if the unit can go on.
NZ if the unit at IX can go on: alive ($08 not 0) and with action points ($06).
Keep the unit's square ($5D40), action points ($5D42) and facing ($5D43), for undoMove.
Put the unit back where keepPlace kept it: its square, action points and facing, the view and its panel. $5D37 is set; NZ.

A line across the map, words: the start's column ($7091) and row ($7093), the end's column ($7095) and row ($7097), the current column ($7099) and row ($709B), the run across ($709D) and down ($709F), the steps down ($70A1) and across ($70A3), 1 or -1, the minor steps down ($70A5) and across ($70A7), the error ($70A9), the major run ($70AB), the minor run ($70AD), a word unused ($70AF), and the distance so far ($70B1), 2 for each straight step and 3 for each diagonal.
The line's error moves on by the minor run; NC, and the major run taken off it, when it reaches the major run.
Set the line up from its two ends: the runs and steps, which way is the major one, and the error at half the major run.
A step along the line: along the major way, or diagonally when the error runs over; the distance grows by 2 or 3.
Take the units of side A off the map, their floors put back, from the table at $5C50: four bytes a unit, its side (3 for none), its row, its column, and the floor under it.
Put every unit in the table at $5C50 on the map.
Whether the line from ($5D47) to ($5D49) is clear for flag 4 of the squares (lineClear).
The same for flag 2.

Whether the line from the square at $5D47 (row, column) to the one at $5D49 is clear for flag 1, sight: every square on it but the last has its flags (the byte at $D2FF plus what the square holds) tested against the mask in $5D4B. Z when the line reaches its end; NZ where it is blocked, with that square in DE.
List the enemies the unit at ($5D24) can see (seenFrom): the side not in $B712.
List every unit but itself ($5D26) that the unit at ($5D24) can see.

List from $5B97, three bytes each (row, column, number) and $FF at the end, the units of the sides in $5D4D (bit 0 side 0, bit 1 side 1), all but unit ($5D4C), to which the line from the square at $5D51 is clear both ways.

Where the square at $5D49 lies from the one at $5D47 for the unit at IX by its facing ($21): A = 0 in front, 1 to the right, 2 behind, 3 to the left; Z in front. $5D55 and $5D56 are the distances down and across; each facing has its routine, through the table at $7351, and facings 4 to 7 turn the answer of 0 to 3 about.
The routines for facings 0 to 7.
Facing down: facing up's answer, turned about.
Facing down and left: up and right's, turned about.
Facing left: right's, turned about.
Facing up and left: down and right's, turned about.
Front for behind and right for left: A XOR 2.
Facing up: in front if the square is above and no further across than down, behind if below; otherwise to the left or the right.
Facing right: in front if the square is to the right and no further down than across.
Facing up and right: in front if the square is no lower and no further left.
Facing down and right: in front if the square is no higher and no further left.

Of the enemies listed from $5B97, those in front of the unit at IX (inView) are put on the map and listed from $5CA0, and counted in $5D59. In the computer's turn each is marked in the table at $B63A by its number, with ($5DF8).
Make the table at $5C50 again from the map: every unit found on it, with its square and the floor it covers.
Unit A's entry in the table at $5C50: its side (bit 0 of its $25), its square ($5D24) and the floor under it ($16).
$5D24 = the row and $5D25 the column of the map's square at HL.
The enemies in sight when seenCount last showed them.

In a player's turn, the number of enemies in sight ($5D59) in the panel, with message $17, or the blank (message $16) when there are none. When more are in sight than before, the view is drawn again and the line flashes seven times with sound effect 7.

Reaction fire. When enemies see the unit that moved ($5D33, the list from $5B97 copied to $5BD1) and it does not stand on a unit, the sides swap, and each enemy in turn that faces it, has more action points left than half its $05 less one, and has not reacted this turn (the list from $5C3C) is shown and may fire: the computer's through the scenario's hook at $B624, a player's through $8E09. Then the sides swap back, and the unit that moved is shown again.
The sides swapped back, the unit that moved selected again.
The map as side ($B712) sees it: every unit put on it, the other side's taken off, and each enemy that one of the side's units can see in front of it put back. IX is left on the unit at $5D33.
Move the view along the line from the square at $5D69 to the one at $5D6B, a square at a time, centred on each (centreAt), unless the two are the same.
Take every unit off the map.
In a player's turn, wait for fire, each turn adding one to $5D9C; then sound effect 0. BC is kept.

After a turn or a step: sound effect 4 in a player's turn, the panel, and the unit's place kept (keepPlace) unless another unit of its side shares its square (shared). With no action points left on a shared square, it goes back where it was kept (undoMove). NZ while it has points left.
A step back onto a square where a unit stands unseen: the unit is put on the map, which blocks the step, and the view drawn again.

List from $5B79 the objects unit ($5D26) carries, three bytes each: the object's number in the scenario's list (from 1), its kind and its ammunition; $5D8F counts them. The scenario's objects are listed from the address in $B72A, ($B639) of them, six bytes each: the kind (an object of the map, $6E on, or 0 for none), the row and column, the floor under it, its ammunition or charge, and the unit carrying it (0 for none). A unit's $17 is the object in its hands, $23 its kind and $24 its ammunition. IX is kept.
Z if an object of kind A is in the list from $5B79, $5D6F then its entry; NZ if not.
A line of the unit's menu: option A, and its words, message A + $1C.

The unit's menu, fire held with a unit selected. Line 0, done, is always there; unless the unit stands on a unit, 1 fire (with an object in its hands), 2 change what it holds (when it carries any), 3 pick up (with objects on its square) and 4 drop (holding one), which bits 2 and 1 of its $25 can take away; 5 and 6 by the kind of what it holds (its $00 bit 1 with ammunition for it carried; bit 3 not yet primed); 7 to 10 by the terrain in front of it (its $08: 1 a door that opens, 7, and locks with the key it holds, 8; 2 one that closes, 9; 3 one that unlocks with the key, 10); and 11. Then 12, cancel, and the scenario's hook at $B633. The choice runs its routine from the table at $79D1. NZ while the unit can go on.
The routines of the unit's menu, by option, and the scenario's hook at $B636 for option 13.
Option 0, done: the unit is let go, with Z and past the menu's own return (a return address dropped), unless it shares a square with no points left, when it goes back (undoMove).
Option 12, cancel: nothing.
Options 7 and 9, open or close the door in front (IY its terrain's record, $5D3E its square), for a fifth of the unit's most action points ($05): the square becomes the terrain's $09.
Options 8 and 10, lock or unlock it with the key held, for a quarter: the square becomes the terrain's $0B.

Option 2, change what the unit holds, for a quarter of its most action points: the screen cleared, the list of what it carries, and the one chosen into its hands. Choosing none empties its hands, and the points spent are added to its $22.

The list from $5B7A on the screen, a line every two rows from row 4: each object's tile and its name, its ammunition (when its kind's $00 has bit 1 or 5 set) or its fuse (bit 3; $FF shows message $66), its weight ($01 of the kind) and its size ($02). IX is kept.
Choose from the list on show: down and up move the mark ($5D72, 0 for none at the top, round from the end), with sound effect 1; fire takes it, with sound effect 2.
Take the mark off: a space in double height.
Draw the mark, a ':' in double height in white.
The mark's place: column 0, row 2 x ($5D72) + 2.
Drop what the unit holds without asking ($5D90 set).

Option 4, drop what the unit holds, for a tenth of its most action points: the object left on its square with the floor under it. On terrain whose $08 is 9, which takes objects smaller than its $09, the player is asked first. Then the largest object on the square (objectAt) is what the unit stands on, and its load is worked out again.

Option 3, pick up, for a quarter of the unit's most action points (a half when its hands are full): the objects on its square listed, and the one chosen into its hands, if its weight ($01) and size ($02) with the rest of what it carries stay under the unit's strength ($14, against half the weight) and its own size ($26); messages $2B and $2C if not. Again while it has the points for another.
List from $5B79 the objects lying on the square in HL (L the row, H the column), at most ten, the way listCarried does, and $5D23 the floor under them. IX is kept.
The weight ($5D91) and size ($5D92) of everything unit ($5D26) carries. IX is kept.
A = the kind of the largest object (its $02) lying on the square in HL, which is the one the map shows; 0, and Z, for none.

The unit's load slows it: $19 is half of its own most action points ($1B) times the weight it carries over its strength ($14), each step rounded (div32, div32Round); its most action points ($05) are $1B less that, and its points are cut to them.

A step the way A. Off the map: Z. Then by what stepCost found in $5D29: stepping back onto a unit, or 3, nothing; 0, an enemy ahead, close combat ($80CD); 1, $7F0B; 5, the step (makeStep) and the panel; anything else, message $14 and the unit's numbers. NZ while the unit can go on.

Close combat against the terrain in front ($5D29 is 1): the attack's strength and price (attackStats; too few points, message $2D), the damage rolled, the terrain broken by it and the square drawn again, victory points for the damage, the fires it starts ($99E8), then the view centred on the unit, the enemies it sees, the reactions to it and whether the game is over. NZ while the unit can go on.
The view's corner put on the unit's square and the cursor at 0, so that centreOnUnit centres the view on it.
Too few action points for the attack: message $2D, the unit's numbers again, and $5D37 set. NZ.
PRINT_ROW and PRINT_COL = the place on the screen of the map's square ($5D3A) in the view: twice its row and column in the view, plus one.
The blow on the screen: sound effect 9, and over the square in front the scenario's tiles listed from $B64E to an $FF, in white, each with the sound played; then the square drawn again.

The attack's strength in $5D98, its skill in $5D97 and its price in $5D9A: the unit's most action points ($05) over a divisor, rounded. $5D35 = the points left after, and C if they would run out. Armed: an object in its hands whose kind ($23) has bit 0 of its $00 set. The divisor is the kind's $04; the strength is the kind's $06 plus the unit's strength ($14) over the kind's $07; the skill the kind's $05 plus the unit's $15 over the kind's $08.
Bare-handed: the divisor 5, the strength the unit's $13, the skill twice its $15.

The terrain at ($5D3A) broken by a blow of strength $5D98. While the blow left ($5D99) is at least the terrain's $03, the square becomes the terrain's $04, the terrain's $07 is added to the damage done ($5D8C), and the blow loses the terrain's $05. $5D27 is the terrain left.
Terrain whose $08 is 7 catches fire: its $09 and the square go in the entry of the list of fires at ($5DF3) when that is free, and ($5DF3) moves on, round to $5CB3 at the $FF that ends the list.
The damage of the blow, in $5D98: a random number from 0 to the strength, plus half the strength; at most $FF.

A = a random number below ($5D9B): the refresh register R, plus the byte at ($5D9D), which moves on a byte each try, plus $5D9C, the count of the turns of the waits for a key. Tried again until it is below. HL is kept. With ($5D9B) 0 the RET Z returns to the address in HL, still on the stack. The limits the game gives are never 0.

Close combat against the enemy in front ($5D29 is 0, its record at $5D3C): the attack's strength and price (too few points, message $2D), the damage rolled and the blow drawn; then the readout: message $3E, the weapon's name (message $3F bare-handed), the chance, the points it costs, and the side it lands on (message $40 plus $5D9F).
The chance is the skill less the defender's $15, all of it from in front, half from the side and a quarter from behind (armourHit finds the side). It is shown with a '%'.

A random number from 0 to 99 below the chance is a hit: the damage shown and taken off, the views and the bottom line drawn again, the death of a defender left with no health, sound effect 3. Otherwise message $44, a miss.
A pause, the points paid, and whether the game is over, whose flags are returned.

The blow against the defender ($5D3C). The floor it stands on takes its $06 off the strength: none left, no damage, and IX stays the attacker. Then the side of the defender it lands on, $5D9F (inView from the attacker's square $5D24: 0 the front, 1 a side, 2 behind); the defender's armour on that side ($0D, $0E or $0F) takes its value off the damage, and loses half of what is left. The damage is at most the defender's health ($08). IX = the defender.
No damage: $5D98 = 0.
The damage ($5D98) off the health ($08) of the unit at IX. Left with none it dies ($8229).
BIT 4,(IX+$25) then OR A: the OR sets the flags again by the damage, which is not 0 here, so the RET NZ is always taken.
Never reached: a unit hurt and in play was to lose morale ($0C), its morale over its most health ($07) over the damage, rounded.

The unit at IX ($5D39 its number on the map) dies. It leaves the table of units; what it carries is left on its square ($5D3A, on the floor in $5D23), and destroyed when its $25 has bit 3 set. Its square becomes its body ($03), which is added to the scenario's objects. The other side scores its $27 in victory points, morale moves on both sides by its $01 ($829E), and $98AE = $6E.
Morale after a loss: every unit in play ($25 bit 4 clear) of side $5DA0 gains A ($5DA1) of morale ($0C), up to its most ($0B); every unit of the other side loses as much. IX is kept.
Byte B of the record at HL gains A, up to $FF and up to the byte before it. HL is kept.
Byte B of the record at HL loses A, down to 0. HL is kept.
Add an object of kind A at ($5D3A), on floor $5D23 and carried by unit C, in the first free entry of the scenario's objects. None free: A = 0, with Z.
Number A at the place in HL with a '%' after it, in double height when $5D09 has bit 3 set.
NZ, and the unit's numbers shown, when the unit at IX has action points and health left.
The hit on the screen: for every four points of damage, the scenario's tiles $B653 and $B654 over the square in front in yellow, with sound effect 9, and the square drawn again.

The death on the screen: sound effect 12; the unit in front ($5D3C) spun round twice until it faces down, with sound effect 10 at each turn; then the three tiles of the falling body, from the scenario's table at ($B720), four bytes for each kind of unit ($00): the colours and the three tiles.
The view moved along to the next unit of the side whose turn it is after unit $5DA2, round from 19 to 0. NZ for none.
Eight bytes nothing reads.
The scanner's dot at pixel row ($5DA3) plus 8 and column ($5DA4) plus 8: set ($5DA6 0, and $5DA5 = what was there), cleared (1) or flipped (2).

Option 3 of cursor mode, the strategic scanner: the screen cleared to blue with message $45 and the scenario's messages $A0 and $A1 at the bottom right; a frame round the map; every square of the 80 by 50 drawn as the pattern its byte names in the table at $D2FF (bits 3 to 7, 0 for none), three pixels apart from pixel row 9 and column 1; the two keys of the colours.
Then until fire: every 100 reads of the controls, the units' squares and the view's frame are flipped on or off. Fire goes back to the view.
Pattern A (from 1) at pixel row ($5DA7) and column ($5DA8): its dots, a row and a column from there each, listed to an $FF from the address at $85F9 + 2 x (A - 1).
The scanner's 21 patterns: where each one's dots are listed.
The patterns' dots: a row and a column for each, from 0 to 2, and $FF at each pattern's end.
The view's frame on the scanner, flipped: a square of 33 dots a side round its eleven squares.
Option 1 of cursor mode: the record of the unit under the cursor ($5D2F its square).

The record of unit $5DA9 on a screen of its own: its tile, turned to face down, and its name; its armour on each side round it ($0D front, $0E right, $0F rear, $10 left) and its $11; then eight bars from $5B00, two bytes each, the most and the value, each with its value: weapon skill ($12), close combat ($13), agility ($15), strength ($14), constitution ($07 and $08), action points ($1B and $06), morale ($0B and $0C), stamina ($09 and $0A). Fire goes back to the view. IX is kept.
The tile is drawn through the table of squares at $E65F, a byte before the usual one.
Number A at ($5D6D), and ($5D6D) two rows down.

The eight bars of the record. For each, from $5B00, its outline as long as its most plus two, from pixel column $78 and rows $3A on, $10 apart; from $7F up, the most and the value are halved first. Then the bars are filled a column at a time, $80 steps with a short wait each, each as far as its value.
A line of twelve dots down from pixel row ($5DAC).
C = 8 x A over B, rounded down; 0, with Z, for B = 0.

The shot's dot at ($5DA3, $5DA4) added to its trail, a ring of 44 places from $5B00 to the $FE at $5B58 ($5DB2 the next): the dot is set, $5DA5 then saying whether something was drawn there already, which stops the shot; the oldest dot of the trail is taken off.

The shot's flight along the line from ($7091, $7093) to ($7095, $7097), in pixels of the map, a dot at a time with its sound. The view scrolls when the dot reaches one of its edges. The flight stops at the map's edge ($5DB7), at a dot already drawn on the screen ($5DA5) or at the weapon's range ($70AF, the dots so far in $70B1). Then the trail is taken off, a dot at a time. What a shot hits is found from the screen: the first dot of its line that something has drawn already.
C while the dots so far ($70B1) are fewer than the range ($70AF).
The trail taken off, a dot at a time with the shot's sound.
The trail emptied: $FF from $5B00 to $5B57.

The shot at the right-hand edge of the view: the view moved eleven squares right ($5DB6), or as far as the map goes, the dot with it, the trail emptied and the view drawn again. At the map's edge $5DB7 is set and the shot stops.
The same at the left-hand edge.
The same at the bottom.
The same at the top.
The crosshair's 21 dots: a row and a column from the cursor's pixel each.
The crosshair flipped on or off, its dots from $8B50 round the cursor's pixel ($5D11 down, $5D12 across).
The crosshair's place on the map in pixels, sixteen to a square: $5DC9 across, $5DCB down.

A missed shot's end moved off the coordinate in $5DD2 by $5DD0 over eight over a random number (from $14, the range of it larger for a shot with a better chance, $5DCD), rounded; one way or the other, and not below 0. HL is the coordinate.
The map's square of the shot's dot ($7099 across, $709B down, in the view): its square in the view in $5D11 and $5D12, on the map in $5D3A, its address in $5D3E.
The map's square under the crosshair ($5D49) and what is there (HL); Z if it is the unit firing ($5D26).

Into fire mode: the cursor kept off ($B71B), the view and the cursor saved ($5DBC, $5DC0), the cursor turned into pixels, sixteen to a square from the middle ($5DBE, $5DBF), and the line's start on the map ($7091, $7093, kept in $5DD8 and $5DD6).

The shots of the weapon ($5DC2 its kind) for this unit: the chances of auto ($5DDF), snap ($5DE1) and aimed ($5DE3) fire are the kind's $0E, $0A and $0C plus a quarter, a half and all of the unit's weapon skill ($12) over the kind's $13 (when its $00 has bit 1 set), at most 100.

Their prices in action points: eight times the unit's most ($05) over the kind's $0D, $09 and $0B, with no auto fire when $0D is 0. A throw's chance is the unit's agility ($15) and its price a fifth of its most points; none when its $25 has bit 1 set.
A + B, at most 100.

The readout in fire mode: message $4C, the weapon's name ($5DE7), the unit's points and ammunition, and for each of the four shots from $5DDF its chance with a '%' and its price, or message $4D for a shot it has not.
The unit's action points ($06) and the ammunition in its weapon ($24) in the readout.

Option 1 of the unit's menu, fire, with the weapon in its hands ($23 its kind, kept in $5DE7, its record in $5DC2). The crosshair moves until fire. A square outside the unit's field of view (inView) gives message $67. Any other square but the unit's own gives the menu of the shots it has (0 auto, 1 snap, 2 aimed, 3 throw), the record of a unit under it (4, $5DA9), 5 end fire and 6 cancel, their routines in the table at $8EE5.
Fire mode ends when the unit dies, or by option 5, which returns past the unit's menu too.
The routines of the fire menu, by option.
Option 6, cancel: nothing.

Option 5, the end of fire mode: the cursor back on ($B71B), the table of squares as it was ($B718, $B716), the view and the cursor put back and the view drawn. In a player's turn it returns past its caller, with Z.
Option 4, the record of the unit under the crosshair.
The sound of a dot of the shot: clicks of the speaker closer each time ($5D7B, by 3 up to $D2) until their sum ($5D7C) reaches $D2, with a noise from the refresh register R; then a short wait.
One round of auto fire: its chance ($5DDF) and its price ($5DE0).
Option 2, an aimed shot: its chance ($5DE3) and its price ($5DE4).
Option 1, a snap shot: its chance ($5DE1) and its price ($5DE2).

A shot of chance $5DCD and price B: the price paid (payAP), a round of ammunition used; the range, the cursor kept, the line from the unit to the crosshair, the chance (a miss moves the line's end), the flight and what it hits, a pause, and the unit's points.
A round from the weapon in the unit's hands (the scenario's object $17, its $04, and the unit's $24). None left: message $4E, and Z.
The shot's range in $70AF: sixteen times the weapon's $12.
The cursor ($5DC7) and the view ($5DC5) kept.
The line's end at the crosshair ($7095, $7097).

The shot starts from the unit: the view as it was when fire mode began, the dot at the unit's pixel ($5DBE, $5DBF), the view drawn with tile 0 over the unit's square (so that the shot does not stop at the unit's own dots), the trail emptied and no dots flown yet ($70B1).

The chance: a random number from 0 to 99 below it ($5DCD) is a hit, with C, and the line stays. A miss by more moves the line's end ($7095, $7097): each way by up to the distance ($5DCE, the longer of the two differences doubled plus the shorter) times half the miss plus one ($5DD0), over a random number (scatter).

The shot flies; when it stops at something drawn, what is there is hit. An explosive weapon (its kind's $00 has bit 2 set) bursts ($91A2). Otherwise the sparks at the dot and the damage of the weapon's $0F rolled (attackRoll); terrain is broken, with its victory points and its fires, the views and the scenario's hook at $B627; a unit takes the blow ($9175). Then whether the game is over.

A shot hits unit A: its record in $5D3C, its armour on the side it lands on, the hit shown and the damage taken, the bottom line, the death of a unit left with no health, the view and sound effect 3; then whether the game is over.
An explosive shot bursts: on the square before a wall on the line ($9A47), with the strength of the weapon's $0F ($968E) round it ($9696), its fires, and whether the game is over.

After a shot: the unit's points ($5D35), and half the price (in $6D4D, which payAP wrote) added to its $22; the cursor and the view back. In a player's turn the view drawn and the scenario's hook at $B627; a dead unit sets $5DE8. NZ.

Victory points for the damage done to terrain ($5D8C): to side 0 when the scenario's $B704 is set, to side 1 when $B705 is, each with the morale shock of it ($829E). $5D4D is set to the side, but moraleShock goes by $5DA0, the side of the last unit killed.

Option 0, auto fire, a burst along a line. Too few points for three rounds: message $14. The first point is under the crosshair and the second chosen after it (message $4F; outside the field of view, message $67), each with the chance applied (shotHit). Then the rounds are chosen (message $50, from 3 to as many as the points pay for), and the burst fired ($9360).

Choose the rounds ($5D86, shown at $5D89): one way (bit 1 of the controls) counts up, round from the most ($5D88 less one) to 3 ($5D87); the other (bit 2) counts down, round the other way. Fire takes it, with sound effect 2.

The burst. For each round: its price paid and its ammunition used; the line's end moved along from the first point ($5D80, $5D7E) to the second ($5D84, $5D82) by the round's share of the way (div32, div32Round); the flight and what it hits. It stops when the points or the ammunition run out, or the unit dies.
BC = 32 x A divided by B, rounded down; 0, with Z, for B = 0.
DE = 32 x HL divided by BC, rounded to the nearest; 0, with Z, for BC = 0.
The remainder against half of BC: at least half rounds up.

Sparks: ($5DDA) of them from pixel ($5DDB, $5DDC), each a cross of five dots flipped off and on as it moves by its step in the table at $954E, and back to the start from $AC; ($5DDE) moves, each dot with a click of noise from the refresh register R. Unless $5DDD is set, the view's colours fade every fourth move ($99B9), down to $42.
A cross of five dots flipped, round ($5DA3 + 1, $5DA4 + 1).
The sparks, four bytes each: the step down and across, and the place.
The blast's strength ($968E) and size ($968F), the box it covers ($9690 to $9693) and its centre ($9694, $9695).

A blast of strength ($968E) at ($9694, $9695). In the computer's turn its units are taken off the map first. The view is centred on the blast. The box five squares round it ($9690 to $9693, inside the map) gets a table of 11 x 11 from $5B00: the strength reaching each square, along a line from the centre to every square of the box's edge ($980E), the centre at full strength.
Then every square of the box takes its blow ($98AF); the view flashes, the sparks fly, the units are shown again, and whether the game is over.

The blast along the line from its centre ($7091 across, $7093 down) to ($7095, $7097). At each square ($5D3A) the strength left ($968F) is kept in the table where it is the most so far, and the terrain there takes its toll ($9868). Each step costs a sixteenth of the blast's strength, and the line ends when nothing is left.
The strength left ($968F) kept at the square $5D3A of the table when it is the most so far; then the square's terrain, and each terrain it becomes when broken, takes off its $05.
HL = the place in the table from $5B00 of the square $5D3A: 11 to a row, from the box's corner ($9690, $9692).
What stood on the square the blast is breaking; $6E after a unit dies.

The blow of the strength in the table on the square $5D3A: the terrain broken (breakTerrain) with its victory points, and the map changed ($98AE what was there, $5D23 the floor). The first unit standing there takes the blow (armourHit, takeDamage).
Every object lying there is destroyed when the strength is at least its kind's $11. When an object stood on the map there, the largest left (objectAt, $5D96) is put back on it.
The view's colours, 22 by 22 from $5821, all A. BC is kept.
The list of fires from $5CB3 emptied, $5DF1 and $5DF3 at its start, and $5CEF = $FF.
The fires in the list at ($5DF1) set off one after another, each a blast of its strength at its square, until an empty entry; the list's start wraps round at its $FF.
NZ if a unit of the side whose turn it is ($B712), other than unit $5D26, stands on the square $5D24: a unit may not end its move on another's square.

Where an explosive shot bursts: of the eight squares round the one it hit ($5D3A), the nearest to the unit firing ($5D24) whose byte in the table at $D2FF has bit 1 clear, which a blast passes; $5D3A and $5D3E then that square. None such: the square hit.

Option 3 of fire mode, throw what the unit holds (its kind's entry at ($5DC2)): the chance ($5DE5) and the action points ($5DE6) paid first. It goes half the distance to the crosshair, at most the unit's strength ($14) over the object's weight ($01), along the line a shot would take. Where it comes down on a unit that faces the thrower and has its hands free, with fewer than ten things carried, it is caught (message $51 and the catcher's name); otherwise it falls on the square, and on one whose byte in the table at $D2FF has bit 1 set (a wall) it falls on the nearest open square instead. Either way the thrower's hands are empty and fire mode ends.
The distance in squares times 32, the length of the flight the shot routines draw.
Where the flight stopped: a square, or a unit ($8C or more).
It falls: left on the square, out of the thrower's hands, shown, and a pause.
A unit is there: it catches the throw if the thrower is in front of it ($7326 answers 0) and it holds nothing ($17).
The catcher's list of what it carries ($785D) must have room: fewer than ten.
Caught: the thrower's held kind, ammunition and object pass to the catcher, the object is placed under the catcher and given to it as owner.
A NOP: one byte left where an instruction was taken out.
The thrower holds nothing, and fire mode ends ($8EF4).

The object in the unit's hands ($17) left at the square ($5D3A) on its floor, carried by nobody. The map square shows it ($5DE7); where a unit stands there, the unit's square-under ($16) becomes the object's tile instead. IY is left at the object's entry.

Option 6 of the unit's menu, prime what it holds, for a fifth of the unit's most action points ($05). The timer is chosen with message $55, from 0 to $28 half-turns; the half-turn it goes off is the timer plus twice the turn ($B711) plus the side ($B712), stored in the object's $04 and the unit's $24.

The timed explosives go off: every object whose kind has bit 3 of its $00 set (a timer) and whose half-turn ($04) is this one, the turn ($B711) and the side ($B712), explodes where it lies, or where the unit carrying it ($05) stands: a blast of its kind's strength ($0F) at that square ($9696), the fires it starts ($99E8) and a long pause. The object stays in the list.

Option 5 of the unit's menu, reload, for half the unit's most action points, which are added to its points spent ($22). The clip ($5D6F points at its entry in the list of what the unit carries) is used up and removed, and the weapon's ammunition, the unit's $24 and the object's $04, set to the clip kind's $10. Message $56 and a pause.

The side ($B712) equips its units: its price list ($B685, or $B6A3 for the second side) in $5DEE, its credits ($B6F8 + side) and message $58; its units listed; the armour table and each unit's armour chosen in turn. Then the shop: the top line picks a kind of object with left and right, and on a unit's line right buys it one and left sells one back. Fire, and fire again, ends it.
Up and down move the lit line ($5D2B, 0 the top line, then one per unit, round).
Fire: message $59, and fire again to finish; any other control goes back to the shop.
Pay A from the side's credits ($B6F8 + side) if they are enough: the credits left shown at row 0, column $1D, and the carry set. Not enough: nothing paid, the carry clear.

The side's units are listed from $5B00 ($5D2C counts them): those whose flags at $B6E4 + number have the side's bit (1 for the first, 2 for the second) and that are in the game ($25 bit 7 clear). Each gets a line with its name and its tile, and everything it carried is taken from it.
$5D2F is set from the word at $5D2C, its low byte just cleared: nothing reads it here.
The armour table: message $5A, and the 28 bytes from $B6C8 as numbers, seven to a column from row 9 (rows $0D and $10 left out) and four columns from column $14.

Each unit listed chooses its armour, 0 to 4, on its lit line ($6918). The type's seven bytes at $B6C1 + 7 x type give the unit's front ($0D), left ($10), right ($0E) and rear ($0F) armour, its $11 (taken from its action points every turn), its room to carry ($26), and the price, paid ($9E27) when the credits are enough. The carry is not looked at: a unit gets its armour whether it was paid for or not.
What the unit on line $5D2B carries, drawn along its row from column $0C, and the rest of the row's ten squares blank; $5DF5 counts the objects.
Ten rows of ten blank squares, from row 4, column $0C, where the units' objects are drawn.

On the top line: right ($5D2A bit 3 clear) goes to the next kind of object ($6E to $8B, round), left (bit 4) to the one before, passing over the kinds the side may not buy (a price of $FF); the new kind is shown.
The side's price for kind A, from its list at ($5DEE), in $5DF0; Z for $FF, a kind it may not buy.
The kind on offer ($5DED): its tile, its name and its price.
On a unit's line: right buys, left sells.

Buy one of the kind on offer for the unit on the lit line. It must carry fewer than ten things; half the weight it would carry, plus ten, must be less than its strength ($14), or message $5C; and the size it would carry must be less than its armour's room ($26), or message $5D.

The object takes the first free entry of the list, short of the last sixteen, when the credits pay for it. A timed explosive's fuse is set to $FF (off); a kind with bit 5 of its $00 has its own $10 rounds; a kind with bit 1 has the rounds of the kind its $10 names (its clip).
$5D26 = the unit on line $5D2B.
Sell back one object of the kind on offer that the unit on the lit line carries: its entry freed and its price ($5DF0) put back with the side's credits.

One player or two (message $5E). Two: the units of mode 1 play. One, against the computer: its level, 1 to ($B684) (message $5F), which sets the computer's skill ($5DF8, from $B655) and the first side's credits ($B6F8, from $B6FA); the units of mode level + 1 play, and $B706 says the computer has the second side.
A choice from the menu on the screen, as $A276, where fire gives 0 as well.
A choice from the menu on the screen: a number key from 1 to ($5DF6) gives A = 1 to ($5DF6). Sound effect 0; Z for 0.
The keys 1 to 7, as the ROM's KEY-SCAN numbers them.
The units that do not play in mode A, those whose byte at $B670 + number lacks bit A - 1, are taken out of the game ($25 bit 7 set).

The units in the game whose turn to arrive ($1C) is this one ($B711) come on, each on a square at random in its patch: row $1D plus 0 to $1E - 1, column $1F plus 0 to $20 - 1, tried again while a unit stands there or its terrain is closed to the unit ($FF in its cost column, $04).
Set while the units are placed.

The side places its units, each one it places itself (bit 2 of its flags at $B6E4 + number) that is in the game: message $60 with the side's number, the unit's name and what it carries. The cursor moves until fire on one of the side's own squares, listed at $B65E (the code on the map, the side, and the floor it is under the unit).
Every square of the map that is one of the side's squares for placing ($B65E) becomes its floor.

Whether the game is over. A side with no units left gives the other the scenario's $B65C (to side 1) or $B65D (to side 0) in victory points. A side with 100 points, or the last turn ($B701) played, ends the game; otherwise NZ.

The end: the screen cleared, the winner's name (the scenario's message $A0 or $A1 after message $62) or message $64 for none, the points at most 100, message $63 and the scores; then a key, and the game starts again at $B1C3.
Z if a unit of side A is in the table of units; NZ if none is left.
The squares the distance is measured between ($A54B, $A54D) and the larger difference ($A54F).
A = the distance from ($A54B, $A54C) to ($A54D, $A54E): twice the larger difference plus the smaller.
The list sortNear sorts.
Sort the list from ($A578), three bytes an entry (row, column, distance), ($5DFD) + 1 entries, by distance: ($5DFD) passes, each bubbling the nearest up from the end.
The steps to the eight squares round a square: a row and a column each.
The square measured from ($A5DA), the square round which ($A5DC), and the next step ($A5DE).
The eight squares round ($A5DC), by the steps at $A5CA, listed from $5B00 with their distance from ($A5DA), and sorted nearest first. A square off the map is three $FFs.
The steps are not moved on past a square off the map, so every square after it is off the map too.
The controls, 1 to 4 (message $69): $B0C7 the option, 0 to 3.
The controls chosen: 0 Sinclair joysticks, 1 Kempston joystick, 2 cursor keys, 3 Q, A, O, P and SPACE.
Read the controls by the option chosen, through the readers' table at $B0E0, into $5D2A: a bit each, clear when held: fire 0, up 1, down 2, right 3, left 4.
The readers return here (LD ($5D2A),A; RET), then the readers' addresses.
The Sinclair joysticks: keys 6 to 0 and 1 to 5, the second's bits reversed into the first's order and both together.
The Kempston joystick, port $1F, its bits set when held, turned into the game's order and sense.
The cursor keys, 5 (left), 6 (down), 7 (up), 8 (right) and 0 (fire), and SPACE.
The keys Q (up), A (down), O (left), P (right) and SPACE (fire), the last read at $B153, where the cursor keys' reader ends too.
0 after a load from tape that worked, 1 otherwise.

The tape, for $49DF bytes at $B621 with the flag B: A 1 loads, 2 checks what is in memory against the tape, 0 saves. A load or check that fails shows message $6A, a check that passes message $6B, until a key.
SA-BYTES, in the ROM, returning to $B1AE.
LD-BYTES, in the ROM past its start (the flag in A', the carry for a load), the border white, returning to $B1AE.
After the tape: the border black, and SPACE (BREAK) held is waited for to be let go; then the return address is dropped, so $B15C ends at once with $B15B still 1.
What $B15C was asked: 0, 1 or 2.

The main menu (message $6C), 1 to 6: a scenario's block (flag $63 + choice) loaded from tape, the menu again if it did not load. Choice 4 is a saved game, which goes on from the menu between turns; the others start a new game.
The menu between turns (message $6D): fire plays on; 1 the controls; 2 saves the game (flag $67), every unit put on the map first; 3 leaves for the main menu; 4 checks the saved game against memory.
Sound effect A: its ten bytes from $B531 + 10 x A copied to $B5B3, and played.

Play the effect at $B5B3: ($B5B3) times ($B5B4) passes over four tones, each a wait of its pitch byte ($B5B6, $B5B8, $B5BA, $B5BC) in loops of three and then the speaker's bit in $B5BD turned over; after each of the ($B5B3), each pitch moves on by the byte before it.
